---
title: "How long one worldwide day takes to process"
subtitle: "Where the time went on 14 June 2026, what was changed, and what is left"
author: "EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit"
date: last-modified
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)

# Read-only. Every number and table on this page comes from a CSV file in
# data/, written by benchmarks/day_timing.py and benchmarks/day_compare.py of
# the opdi repository. Nothing here reads S3, a database or a Spark cluster:
# data/_manifest.json records, for each file, the script, the git commit and a
# fingerprint of the source files.
D <- function(f) read.csv(file.path("data", f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                          colClasses = c(step = "character"))

ds_all <- D("day_summary.csv")  # one row per step and round: before and after, how obtained
ds  <- ds_all[ds_all$round == "code", ]      # the round of code changes
dsr <- ds_all[ds_all$round == "settings", ]  # the round of Spark settings
st <- D("step_timings.csv")     # one row per run of a step (label = which run)
sg <- D("stage_timings.csv")    # one row per Spark stage of each run of a step
rc <- read.csv(file.path("data", "result_comparison.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

num <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")

# One value of day_summary.csv, of step_timings.csv, and the executor-seconds
# (sum of the run time of all tasks) of one run of one step.
S  <- function(step, col) ds[ds$step == step, col]
SR <- function(step, col) dsr[dsr$step == step, col]
ST <- function(label, step, col = "seconds") st[st$label == label & st$step == step, col]
ES <- function(label, step) sum(sg$executor_run_s[sg$label == label & sg$step == step])

before_total <- S("total", "before_s")
after_total  <- S("total", "after_s")

# The share of the cores at work, from the scaling rule written in the notes
# of the "total" row ("... / (16 cores x 0.85) ...").
busy <- as.numeric(sub(".*x ([0-9.]+)\\).*", "\\1", S("total", "notes")))

# Scale factors: the 4-hour slice by rows (from step_timings.csv), the
# aircraft sample by its modulus ("hash(icao24) % 12 == 0").
sf_slice <- as.numeric(ST("scaled_new", "01", "scale_factor"))
sample_m <- as.numeric(sub(".*% ([0-9]+) ==.*", "\\1", ST("m12new", "02", "scope")))

# Executor-seconds of a full day with the new code, step by step.
work <- c(
  "01"  = ES("s4new", "01") * sf_slice,
  "02"  = ES("m12new", "02") * sample_m,
  "02a" = ES("m12new", "02a") * sample_m,
  "03"  = ES("v2", "03"),
  "04"  = ES("v2", "04"),
  "04b" = ES("v2", "04b"),
  "09"  = ES("v2", "09")
)
cores_now <- as.numeric(ST("v2", "03", "executors")) * as.numeric(ST("v2", "03", "cores"))
cores_old <- as.numeric(ST("base", "03", "executors")) * as.numeric(ST("base", "03", "cores"))
work_total <- sum(work)

# Result comparison.
R <- function(part, item, col) rc[rc$part == part & rc$item == item, col]
ev <- rc[rc$part == "events", ]
info_n <- as.numeric(sub(" matched events differ", "", R("event field", "info", "note")))
info_types <- ev$item[grepl("info differs", ev$note)]

# The ingestion time of the ADS-C study, for the caution at the end.
pt <- read.csv(file.path("..", "adsc-effect-v1", "data", "processing_time.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = c(step = "character"))
ar <- read.csv(file.path("..", "adsc-effect-v1", "data", "adsc_reports.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

## Summary

Processing one worldwide day of OpenSky data, 14 June 2026, took about
`r num(before_total)` s (`r num(before_total / 3600, 1)` hours) before this
work and about `r num(after_total)` s (`r num(after_total / 3600, 1)` hours)
after it. The gain came from five changes to the code, which removed repeated
or badly spread work, and from running 12 Spark executors instead of 8. The
published results did not change, and the target of one hour per day was not
reached: the work that remains needs more processors than the cluster has, or
a different way of building tracks.

A second round changed only Spark's settings, on the same hardware (one
more executor, fewer shuffle parts, more memory outside each executor's
heap), and made a day run without losing executors. The whole day was then
measured for the first time, every step, through the daily command: about
`r num(SR("total", "after_s"))` s (`r num(SR("total", "after_s") / 3600, 1)`
hours), with the same results with and without executors deleted on purpose
in the middle of it.

## What was measured

The pipeline turns OpenSky position reports into tracks, a flight list and
flight events in a chain of numbered steps (see
[Processing steps](../../content/methods/pipeline.qmd)). It runs on Apache
Spark, which splits each step into **stages** and each stage into **tasks**
that run in parallel. A task runs on an **executor**, a worker process with 2
processor cores and 14 GiB of memory.

The day measured is 14 June 2026, worldwide: `r num(R("flight list", "flights", "after"))`
flights and `r num(R("file flight_events", "rows", "after"))` events. The same
day was run before and after the changes on the OpenSky cluster. "Before" is
the code as it was, with `r ST("base", "03", "executors")` executors
(`r cores_old` cores). "After" is the changed code with
`r ST("v2", "03", "executors")` executors (`r cores_now` cores), the most the
cluster's allowance holds: 30 processors and 192 GiB of memory, of which the
process that directs the work takes 4 processors and 16 GiB.

### Four steps measured, three scaled

Steps 03, 04, 04b and 09 were measured on the full day. Steps 01, 02 and 02a
were not: their full-day output did not fit in the storage available. They were run on part of the day and scaled up:

- Step 01 (read and thin the reports) ran on the first 2 and the first 4
  hours of the day.
- Steps 02 (build the tracks) and 02a (clean them) ran on all the hours that
  step 02 reads, but only for one aircraft in `r sample_m` (and, as a check,
  one in 24), chosen by a hash of the aircraft address.

A small part of a day runs in one or two rounds of tasks, so its own run time
says little about a full day. The scaling therefore uses the
**executor-seconds** of the part: the sum of the run times of all its tasks.
The rule is

> full-day time = executor-seconds of the part × scale factor ÷ (cores × `r busy`)
> \+ time of the stages that run as a single task × scale factor

The scale factor is the share of the day the part stands for:
`r num(sf_slice, 2)` for the 4-hour slice (the day has
`r num(sf_slice, 2)` times as many reports) and `r sample_m` for one aircraft
in `r sample_m`. The cores are those of the run (`r cores_old` before); on
average `r num(100 * busy)`% of them were at work in the full-day steps. For
example, the 4-hour slice of step 01 used `r num(ES("s4base", "01"))`
executor-seconds before the changes, which gives
`r num(ES("s4base", "01"))` × `r num(sf_slice, 2)` ÷ (`r cores_old` × `r busy`) =
`r num(S("01", "before_s"))` s. Steps 01 to 02a were timed with
`r ST("base", "03", "executors")` executors in both versions; the "after"
figure assumes that 12 executors do the same work 1.5 times as fast.

## Time per step

```{r tbl-steps}
#| echo: false
names_ <- c("01" = "read and thin the reports", "02" = "build the tracks",
            "02a" = "clean the tracks", "03" = "flight list",
            "04" = "events and measurements", "04b" = "milestones into the flight list",
            "09" = "published files", "total" = "all steps")
how <- ifelse(grepl("full day", ds$after_scope), "measured on the full day",
       ifelse(grepl("4 h", ds$after_scope), "scaled from a 4-hour slice",
       ifelse(grepl("aircraft", ds$after_scope), paste("scaled from one aircraft in", sample_m),
              ds$after_scope)))
tab <- data.frame(step = ds$step, what = names_[ds$step],
                  before = num(ds$before_s), after = num(ds$after_s), how = how)
kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrl",
      col.names = c("Step", "What it does", "Before (s)", "After (s)", "How the figure was obtained"),
      caption = paste0("Time of each step for 14 June 2026, worldwide. Before: ",
                       ST("base", "03", "executors"), " executors; after: ",
                       ST("v2", "03", "executors"), " executors."))
```

```{r fig-steps}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Time of each step before and after the changes, in seconds. Steps 01, 02 and 02a are scaled from part of the day; the others are measured on the full day."
#| fig-height: 4
x <- ds[ds$step != "total", ]
m <- rbind(before = x$before_s, after = x$after_s)
colnames(m) <- x$step
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
barplot(m, beside = TRUE, col = c("grey70", "steelblue"), border = NA,
        xlab = "Step", ylab = "Time (s)", las = 1,
        legend.text = c("before", "after"),
        args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n"))
```

Steps 04 and 02 took most of the time before, and still do.

## What was slow, and what was changed

The Spark log of each run gives one row per stage, with its run time, number
of tasks and longest task. Reading these rows step by step showed five
causes.

1. **Holding patterns were computed twice.** The start and the end of a
   holding pattern were produced by two branches of one query, and Spark
   computed the whole holding calculation once for each branch. Both events
   are now read from one computation.
2. **A look-ahead to the end of each track was repeated for every report.**
   The holding and FIR-crossing steps asked, for each report, a question
   about all the later reports of its track. Spark re-reads that whole range
   for every report, so the cost grows with the square of the track length.
   The same question is now asked by reading the track backwards, where the
   range grows by one report at a time.
3. **Whole-day tables were written by a single task.** The tracks, the events
   and the measurements of a day were each sent to one task before writing,
   so one task did the work of the whole day. They are now spread over many
   tasks.
4. **A reference table was stored as thousands of small files.** The table of
   airport zones (the map cells around each airport) was 7,783 small files,
   and the flight-list step read it three times, opening every file each
   time. It is now 8 files, read once per step and kept in memory.
5. **The raw archive was read three times.** Step 01 counted the rows, then
   listed the days, then wrote them: three reads of the archive. It now reads
   it once.

Two smaller changes go with these: step 02 now leaves out, before building
tracks, the aircraft that have no report on the day (they cannot have a track
that starts on it), and the flight-list step sends the two end reports of each
track to the airport zones instead of moving both tables.

Finally, the number of executors went from 8 to 12. @tbl-runs separates the
two effects for the steps measured on the full day: the middle column is the
new code with the old number of executors.

```{r tbl-runs}
#| echo: false
steps <- c("03", "04", "04b", "09")
r <- data.frame(
  step = steps,
  base = num(sapply(steps, function(s) ST("base", s))),
  v1 = num(sapply(steps, function(s) ST("v1", s))),
  v2 = num(sapply(steps, function(s) ST("v2", s))),
  es_base = num(sapply(steps, function(s) ES("base", s))),
  es_v2 = num(sapply(steps, function(s) ES("v2", s)))
)
kable(r, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr",
      col.names = c("Step",
                    paste0("Old code, ", ST("base", "03", "executors"), " executors (s)"),
                    paste0("New code, ", ST("v1", "03", "executors"), " executors (s)"),
                    paste0("New code, ", ST("v2", "03", "executors"), " executors (s)"),
                    "Executor-seconds, old code", "Executor-seconds, new code"),
      caption = "The steps measured on the full day, in three runs.")
```

With the same 8 executors, the new code took step 04 from
`r num(ST("base", "04"))` s to `r num(ST("v1", "04"))` s and step 03 from
`r num(ST("base", "03"))` s to `r num(ST("v1", "03"))` s; the 12 executors
then brought them to `r num(ST("v2", "04"))` s and `r num(ST("v2", "03"))` s.
Step 09 took longer in the middle run (`r num(ST("v1", "09"))` s); this was not
looked into, and it took `r num(ST("v2", "09"))` s in the last run. For the
scaled steps, the 4-hour slice of step 01 fell from
`r num(ES("s4base", "01"))` to `r num(ES("s4new", "01"))` executor-seconds,
and step 02 on one aircraft in `r sample_m` from `r num(ST("m12base", "02"))` s
to `r num(ST("m12new", "02"))` s. Step 02a was not changed; its gain is the
number of executors.

## The results did not change

The outputs of the day before and after the changes were matched flight by
flight and event by event.

```{r tbl-results}
#| echo: false
fl <- rc[rc$part == "flight list" & rc$item == "flights", ]
ms <- rc[rc$part == "measurement", ]
evf <- rc[rc$part == "event field", ]
res <- data.frame(
  what = c("Flights in the flight list",
           "Flights with a different departure or destination airport",
           "Events (all types)",
           "Events matched on flight, type and time",
           "Matched events with a measurement differing by more than 0.000001",
           "Matched events with a different position or altitude",
           "Matched events with a different info text"),
  value = c(num(fl$after),
            num(sum(as.numeric(regmatches(fl$note, gregexpr("[0-9]+", fl$note))[[1]]))),
            num(sum(ev$after)),
            num(sum(ev$matched)),
            num(sum(as.numeric(sub(" matched.*", "", ms$note)))),
            num(sum(as.numeric(sub(" matched.*", "", evf$note[evf$item != "info"])))),
            num(info_n))
)
kable(res, row.names = FALSE, align = "lr", col.names = c("", "After the changes"),
      caption = paste0("The day after the changes compared with the day before. Before: ",
                       num(fl$before), " flights and ", num(sum(ev$before)), " events."))
```

Every flight has the same departure and destination airports, every event is
found again with the same flight, type and time, and every measurement is
equal. The one difference is the `info` text of
`r num(info_n)` events (`r num(100 * info_n / R("event field", "info", "matched"), 1)`%),
all of them airport-surface events and block times
(`r paste0("\x60", info_types, "\x60", collapse = ", ")`). Their `info` names the
taxiway, apron or stand the aircraft is on. Where one map cell lies on two such
parts of the airport, the event names one of them, and which one depended on
the order in which Spark happened to process the rows. That choice also
changed between two runs of unchanged code, so it was not caused by the
changes. The pipeline now always names the part with the smallest
OpenStreetMap identifier (see the next section).

## Are the results the same?

The comparison above counts events and matches them on flight, type and time.
Two further comparisons look at every value.

```{r same-setup}
#| include: false
cc <- read.csv(file.path("data", "content_comparison.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rr <- read.csv(file.path("data", "repeat_run_comparison.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rf <- read.csv(file.path("data", "repeat_run_flight_list.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# One value of a comparison table: the row of a part and an item.
V <- function(df, part, item, col) df[df$part == part & df$item == item, col]
# Columns compared, and columns with at least one matched row differing.
n_cols <- function(df, part) sum(df$part == part & grepl("^column ", df$item))
n_diff_cols <- function(df, part) {
  x <- df[df$part == part & grepl("^column ", df$item), ]
  sum(as.numeric(sub(" matched rows differ", "", x$note)) > 0)
}
# Matched rows with at least one column differing.
n_diff_rows <- function(df, part) {
  as.numeric(sub(" matched rows differ.*", "",
                 V(df, part, "matched rows with a column differing", "note")))
}
rr_ev <- rr[rr$part == "events", ]
adep_p_fl <- as.numeric(sub(" matched rows differ", "",
                            V(rr, "flight_list content", "column adep_p", "note")))
adep_p_ev <- as.numeric(sub(" matched rows differ", "",
                            V(rr, "flight_events content", "column adep_p", "note")))
info_rr <- as.numeric(sub(" matched events differ", "", V(rr, "event field", "info", "note")))
```

**Steps 01 to 02a, before and after the changes.** The code before the
changes and the code after them were run on the same input, and the two
outputs were matched row by row: the reports of step 01 on their aircraft
address and time, the tracks of steps 02 and 02a on their track identifier and
time. For every matched row, every other column was compared, exactly for
text, whole numbers and times, and to within 0.000000001 for decimal numbers.
Step 01 ran on the first 2 hours of 14 June 2026 for all aircraft; steps 02
and 02a on one aircraft in 12, both versions building their tracks from the
same reports.

```{r tbl-same-before-after}
#| echo: false
parts <- c("osn_statevectors_v2", "osn_tracks", "osn_tracks_clean")
what <- c("Step 01: position reports, first 2 hours, all aircraft",
          "Step 02: tracks, one aircraft in 12",
          "Step 02a: cleaned tracks, one aircraft in 12")
g <- function(p, col) as.numeric(V(cc, p, "rows", col))
t1 <- data.frame(
  what = what,
  before = num(sapply(parts, g, col = "before")),
  after = num(sapply(parts, g, col = "after")),
  matched = num(sapply(parts, g, col = "matched")),
  only = paste(num(sapply(parts, g, col = "only_before")), "/",
               num(sapply(parts, g, col = "only_after"))),
  cols = sapply(parts, function(p) n_cols(cc, p)),
  differ = sapply(parts, function(p) n_diff_cols(cc, p))
)
kable(t1, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrr",
      col.names = c("Output", "Rows before", "Rows after", "Matched",
                    "Only before / only after", "Columns compared", "Columns differing"),
      caption = "The code before and after the changes on the same input, row by row.")
```

Every row is found in both outputs, and no value differs. The tracks also have
the same identifiers: `r num(V(cc, "osn_tracks", "track ids", "before"))`
before and `r num(V(cc, "osn_tracks", "track ids", "after"))` after, all of
them in both.

**Steps 03 to 09, two runs of the same code.** The comparison of the full day
before and after the changes cannot be repeated with every value, because the
tables of the run before were deleted for lack of storage. Instead, the code
after the changes was run twice on the full day from the same tracks, and the
two published files were compared value by value. Any difference between two
runs of one code comes from the order in which Spark processes rows, and would
also blur a comparison between two versions.

In both runs the day has `r num(sum(rr_ev$before))` events of
`r nrow(rr_ev)` types, all matched on flight, type and time, and
`r num(V(rr, "flight list", "flights", "before"))` flights. Positions,
altitudes and measurements are the same in all matched events, and the `info`
text differs in `r num(info_rr)` of them: with the fixed choice of the airport
part, it no longer changes from run to run. One
column did differ: `adep_p`, the other airports that could be the departure
airport, for `r num(adep_p_fl)` of the
`r num(V(rr, "flight_list content", "rows", "matched"))` flights (and so in
`r num(adep_p_ev)` events, which carry the flight's columns). The departure
airport itself was the same; only the order of the other airports in the list
changed, because the list was collected in the order Spark met the rows. The
list is now sorted, nearest airport first. Two further runs of the flight list
step with the sorted list gave
`r num(V(rf, "opdi_flight_list", "rows", "matched"))` matched flights of
`r num(V(rf, "opdi_flight_list", "rows", "before"))`, with
`r num(n_diff_rows(rf, "opdi_flight_list"))` differing in any of the
`r n_cols(rf, "opdi_flight_list")` columns compared.

So two runs of the code now give the same flight list and the same events,
value for value, and a future comparison of two versions of the code can be
exact.

## Why one hour was not reached

Adding up the executor-seconds of each step gives the work a day needs with
the new code:

```{r tbl-work}
#| echo: false
w <- data.frame(step = names(work), es = num(work),
                share = paste0(num(100 * work / work_total), "%"))
w <- rbind(w, data.frame(step = "all", es = num(work_total), share = "100%"))
kable(w, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
      col.names = c("Step", "Executor-seconds", "Share"),
      caption = paste0("Work of one worldwide day with the new code. Steps 01 to 02a are scaled as ",
                       "described above, the others measured."))
```

That is about `r num(round(work_total, -3))` executor-seconds. With
`r cores_now` cores at work `r num(100 * busy)`% of the time, it takes about
`r num(work_total / (cores_now * busy))` s, well over the 3,600 s of one hour.
The largest part is step 02, which builds the tracks
(`r num(100 * work[["02"]] / work_total)`%; with the cleaning of step 02a,
`r num(100 * (work[["02"]] + work[["02a"]]) / work_total)`%). To give each
day's tracks their full length, step 02 reads 59 hours of reports for each
day, so every report is split into tracks on two or three different days.

So a day in one hour needs one of two things:

- **More cores.** The work alone asks for about
  `r num(work_total / (3600 * busy))` cores busy `r num(100 * busy)`% of the
  time, against `r cores_now` today; the stages that run as a single task do
  not get faster with more cores, so in practice about twice today's number.
- **A track step that works incrementally**: tracks built once per hour of
  reports, with the tracks still open carried from one day to the next. This
  would remove most of the repeated reading in step 02.

## Spark settings

A second round changed no code of the steps, only the settings of Spark, on
the same hardware: the same namespace allowance of 30 processors and 192 GiB.

```{r settings-setup}
#| include: false
stt <- read.csv(file.path("data", "settings_tests.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                colClasses = c(step = "character"))
xe <- read.csv(file.path("data", "executor_events.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Wall seconds of each run of one step, and their mean.
W  <- function(labels, step) sapply(labels, function(l) as.numeric(ST(l, step)))
MW <- function(labels, step) mean(W(labels, step))
base_runs <- c("pab1", "pab2"); e13_runs <- c("pae1", "pae2")
s104_runs <- c("pas1", "pas2"); kept_runs <- c("pak1", "pak2")
steps4 <- c("03", "04", "04b", "09")
killed <- function(l) as.numeric(xe$killed_137[xe$label == l])
# Comparisons: kept settings against today's (pab2 / pak2), the fault run
# against the undisturbed one (orch3 / orch2), the whole day from the archive
# against the run from the stored tracks (pak2 / orch3).
sk <- read.csv(file.path("data", "settings_events_k.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fi <- read.csv(file.path("data", "fault_injection_comparison.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fu <- read.csv(file.path("data", "full_day_comparison.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
P  <- function(t, part, item, col) t[t$part == part & t$item == item, col]
SK <- function(part, item, col) P(sk, part, item, col)
FI <- function(part, item, col) P(fi, part, item, col)
FU <- function(part, item, col) P(fu, part, item, col)
evsum <- function(t, col) sum(as.numeric(t[t$part == "events", col]))
# The tracks write of step 02 in the five runs on one aircraft in 12.
p1 <- c("p1b1", "p1a1", "p1k1", "p1b2", "p1k2", "p1a2")
wr <- sapply(p1, function(l) sg$seconds[sg$label == l & sg$step == "02" &
                                          grepl("WriteFiles", sg$operators)])
xm <- read.csv(file.path("data", "executor_memory.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
               colClasses = c(step = "character"))
dm <- read.csv(file.path("data", "driver_memory.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
XM <- function(l, st, col) xm[xm$label == l & xm$step == st, col]
spill02 <- sum(sg$spill_disk_bytes[sg$label == "orch3" & sg$step == "02"]) / 1e9
```

Each setting was run twice, alternating with the runs without it, on the same
input: steps 03 to 09 on the full day from the existing tracks, or steps 02
and 02a on one aircraft in 12. A single run proves little here, because the
storage service varies from one run to the next: the same tracks write of
step 02 took `r num(min(wr))` to `r num(sort(wr)[length(wr) - 1])` s in
`r length(wr) - 1` runs and `r num(max(wr))` s in another, and step 03 of the
same settings took `r num(ST("pab1", "03"))` and `r num(ST("pab2", "03"))` s.
A setting was kept only when its gain was clearly larger than that spread,
and only when the results stayed the same (compared event by event and
flight by flight, as in the section above).

```{r tbl-settings}
#| echo: false
s <- stt[stt$runs > 0, c("setting", "value", "step", "wall_s_each", "executor_s_each",
                        "executors_killed_each", "verdict")]
kable(s, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Setting", "Value", "Step", "Time of each run (s)",
                    "Executor-seconds of each run", "Executors killed (exit 137)", "Kept?"),
      caption = "Settings tried on the cluster. Steps 02 and 02a: one aircraft in 12; steps 03 to 09: the full day. The reasons are in data/settings_tests.csv.")
```

What came out:

- **13 executors instead of 12.** The comment in the configuration said a
  13th would wait for memory; it does not. An executor's container is its
  heap plus a share for everything outside it, and 13 containers fit. Step 04
  took `r num(MW(e13_runs, "04"))` s instead of `r num(MW(base_runs, "04"))` s
  (`r num(100 * (MW(e13_runs, "04") / MW(base_runs, "04") - 1))`%).
- **104 shuffle parts instead of 200** (`spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`, 4
  per core). Step 04 keeps each event family in that many parts, most of them
  tiny. Step 04 then took `r num(MW(s104_runs, "04"))` s
  (`r num(100 * (MW(s104_runs, "04") / MW(e13_runs, "04") - 1))`% against 13
  executors with 200 parts).
- **Memory outside the heap.** The configuration named 2 GiB for it, but
  that value never reached the cluster, so Spark used its default of 10% of
  the heap, 1.2 GiB. In every full-day run every executor was killed for
  memory (exit code 137) in step 09, when the Python workers that compute H3
  cells start (`r killed("pab1")` and `r killed("pab2")` executors in the two
  runs with today's settings), and one run failed in step 04b after Spark had
  tried a stage four times. With 11 GiB of heap and 2.5 GiB outside it no
  executor was killed, and step 09 took `r num(MW(kept_runs, "09"))` s instead
  of `r num(MW(base_runs, "09"))` s. The highest use, in step 09, was
  `r num(XM("pak1", "09", "total_rss"))` MiB (Java `r num(XM("pak1", "09", "java_rss"))`,
  Python `r num(XM("pak1", "09", "python_rss"))`) of the 13,824 MiB container;
  over the whole day, `r num(max(xm$total_rss[xm$label == "orch3"]))` MiB. Moving 1 GiB more out of the heap (10 GiB +
  3.5 GiB) made the single task that writes the day's events file run out of
  heap, so 11 + 2.5 GiB stays.
- **Not kept:** the Arrow form of the H3 function (it saves 25 of about
  3,900 executor-seconds of step 02, less than the spread) and the Kryo
  serialiser (no change: the steps work on Spark's own row format). Not run,
  with the reason in `settings_tests.csv`: file packing for reads,
  broadcast thresholds, memory fractions, locality waits and speculative
  copies of slow tasks. The output committer needed no change: Spark 4
  already uses the S3A "magic" committer, which writes without renames.

With all kept settings steps 03 to 09 took
`r num(sum(sapply(steps4, function(s) MW(kept_runs, s))))` s against
`r num(sum(sapply(steps4, function(s) MW(base_runs, s))))` s with today's
settings, and the results were the same: `r num(SK("flight list", "flights", "matched"))`
flights and `r num(evsum(sk, "matched"))` events of
`r sum(sk$part == "events")` types, all matched.

## A whole day, measured

With room in the storage, the whole day was then run from the raw archive,
every step 01 to 09, through the command the daily schedule runs
(`python -m opdi.orchestration day`), with the kept settings. Each working
table was deleted as soon as no later step read it. The reports of the last
11 hours of 13 June, which a daily run finds left by the day before, were
written first; step 01 then fetched 14 and 15 June, so the table below gives
its time per day fetched.

```{r tbl-fullday}
#| echo: false
full <- c("01", "02", "02a", "03", "04", "04b", "09")
fd <- data.frame(step = full,
                 est = sapply(full, function(s) as.numeric(S(s, "after_s"))),
                 run1 = sapply(full, function(s) as.numeric(SR(s, "after_s"))),
                 run2 = sapply(full, function(s) as.numeric(ST("orch2", s))))
# Step 01 of a day fetches one new day; the runs fetched two (14 and 15 June).
fd$run2[1] <- as.numeric(ST("orch2", "01-d1"))
fd <- rbind(fd, data.frame(step = "all", est = sum(fd$est), run1 = sum(fd$run1), run2 = sum(fd$run2)))
kable(transform(fd, est = num(est), run1 = num(run1), run2 = num(run2)), row.names = FALSE,
      align = "lrrr",
      col.names = c("Step", "Estimate after the code changes (s)", "Undisturbed run (s)",
                    "Run with two executors deleted (s)"),
      caption = "One worldwide day, 14 June 2026, every step. Step 01: one day of reports fetched (the daily case). The estimate is the 'after' figure of the first round (12 executors, today's settings; steps 01 to 02a scaled).")
```

A day now takes `r num(SR("total", "after_s"))` s
(`r num(SR("total", "after_s") / 3600, 1)` hours), against the
`r num(S("total", "after_s"))` s estimated after the code changes; a second
undisturbed run gave `r num(ST("orch1", "02"))` s for step 02 and
`r num(ST("orch1", "04"))` s for step 04. Step 01 was estimated well
(`r num(S("01", "after_s"))` s against `r num(SR("01", "after_s"))` s). Steps
02 and 02a were estimated too high, by
`r num(100 * (S("02", "after_s") / SR("02", "after_s") - 1))`% and
`r num(100 * (S("02a", "after_s") / SR("02a", "after_s") - 1))`%. Part of that
is the settings (one more executor, fewer shuffle parts), which were not
measured on these two steps on their own; most of it in step 02a is the
scaling from one aircraft in 12. Step 02 spills about `r num(spill02)` GB to the
executors' local disks with 104 shuffle parts; the next section measures what
that costs.

## Shuffle parts of the track step

```{r partitions-setup}
#| include: false
pt <- read.csv(file.path("data", "partition_tests.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
               colClasses = c(step = "character"))
PT <- function(step, n, col) as.numeric(pt[pt$step == step & pt$shuffle_partitions == n, col])
MP <- function(step, n, col = "wall_s") mean(PT(step, n, col))
```

Step 02 sorts the position reports of each aircraft in time for its window
functions. Spark splits that work into as many parts as
`spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` says, 104 in the settings above, chosen for
step 04. With 104 parts each part of the largest sort is too large for the
memory one task gets, so Spark writes the overflow to the executor's local
disk and reads it back ("spill"). Spilling does not change the result, but
costs time.

The whole day was run through step 02 again from the same reports, with
104, 208, 416 and 832 parts, and the 104, 208 and 416 runs twice. Step 02a
(cleaning), which runs the same kind of sort, was run twice with 104 and
twice with 416 parts on the same tracks. Every run's output was compared row
by row with the first run with 104 parts: the same
`r sub("identical: ([0-9,]+) rows.*", "\\1", pt$content[2])` reports and
`r sub(".* rows, ([0-9,]+) track ids.*", "\\1", pt$content[2])` tracks, every
column equal, in each case (column `content` of the table's file).

```{r tbl-partitions}
#| echo: false
tab <- data.frame(step = pt$step, parts = pt$shuffle_partitions, run = pt$run,
                  wall = num(pt$wall_s), exec = num(pt$executor_s),
                  spill = num(pt$spill_disk_gb, 1),
                  task = paste0(num(pt$largest_stage_task_max_s), " / ", num(pt$largest_stage_task_median_s)),
                  mem = num(pt$peak_executor_memory_mib), disk = num(pt$peak_local_disk_gb, 1),
                  lost = pt$executors_lost)
kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrrrr",
      col.names = c("Step", "Shuffle parts", "Run", "Time (s)", "Executor-seconds", "Spilled to disk (GB)",
                    "Largest sort: longest / median task (s)", "Highest executor memory (MiB)",
                    "Highest local disk of one executor (GB)", "Executors lost"),
      caption = "Steps 02 and 02a of the worldwide day 2026-06-14 with different numbers of shuffle parts, 13 executors. Memory: the container holds 13,824 MiB.")
```

With 104 parts step 02 spilled `r num(PT("02", 104, "spill_disk_gb")[1])` GB to
disk and took `r num(PT("02", 104)[1])` and `r num(PT("02", 104)[2])` s. With
416 parts nothing was spilled and it took `r num(PT("02", 416)[1])` and
`r num(PT("02", 416)[2])` s:
`r num(MP("02", 104) - MP("02", 416))` s or
`r num(100 * (1 - MP("02", 416) / MP("02", 104)))`% less, four times the
difference between two runs with the same setting. 208 parts were as fast
(`r num(PT("02", 208)[1])` and `r num(PT("02", 208)[2])` s), but the busiest
executor came within `r num(13824 - max(PT("02", 208, "peak_executor_memory_mib")))` MiB
of its container's limit, against `r num(13824 - max(PT("02", 416, "peak_executor_memory_mib")))` MiB
with 416; 832 parts were slower again (`r num(PT("02", 832))` s), because the
many small parts cost more to start than they save. Step 02 therefore runs with
416 parts; the other steps keep 104 (`OPENSKY_STEP_SETTINGS` in the
configuration of the opdi repository). Step 02a does not spill with 104 parts,
and with 416 it took `r num(MP("02a", 416))` s instead of `r num(MP("02a", 104))` s,
so it keeps 104.

The spill was a cost in time, not a risk for the disks. An executor's local
folder is a temporary folder of its pod with no size limit of its own; it
lies on the disk of the machine that runs the pod, 527 GB, which every pod on
that machine shares. The most one executor held there, the shuffle files of
the step with or without the spill, was
`r num(max(pt$peak_local_disk_gb), 1)` GB, and the most any of these machines had
in use was `r num(max(pt$node_disk_used_max_gb))` GB. Kubernetes removes pods from
a machine only when its disk is nearly full (by default, less than 10% free,
about 53 GB here), which is far from what a day needs. The local disk was
measured every 15 s, so a spill file written and removed between two readings
is not seen.

The whole day from the archive does not give the same flight list as the
runs above, which started from the tracks stored in the warehouse on 17
October: `r num(FU("flight list", "flights", "after"))` flights against
`r num(FU("flight list", "flights", "before"))`, of which
`r num(FU("flight list", "flights", "matched"))` match, and
`r num(evsum(fu, "matched"))` of `r num(evsum(fu, "before"))` events match.
The differences are at the ends of the tracks (the last report, the landing
and the arrival airport), which points at the tracks stored in October,
built by the code of that time; they were not traced further here. The
comparisons of settings above all start from the same stored tracks.

## Does a day finish unattended?

The same full-day command was run with faults put in on purpose: one
executor was deleted (`kubectl delete pod`) in the middle of step 02 and
another in the middle of step 04. Both steps finished without being
restarted, Spark re-ran the lost work, and the outputs were the same as those
of the undisturbed run: `r num(FI("flight list", "flights", "matched"))`
flights and `r num(evsum(fi, "matched"))` events, all matched, with
`r num(evsum(fi, "only_before") + evsum(fi, "only_after"))` events in one run
only. The two deletions cost
`r num(ST("orch2", "02") - ST("orch3", "02"))` s in step 02 and
`r num(ST("orch2", "04") - ST("orch3", "04"))` s in step 04.

What made that possible, besides the memory above: the frames step 04 keeps
in the executors' memory are now held twice, so losing one executor no longer
loses them (before, the step failed); each step that fails for a passing
reason (the storage refusing requests, a lost upload, lost executors) is run
again by the command, up to twice, in a new Spark session; a day of reports
counts as fetched only when its fetch is recorded as finished; and reading a
table left empty by a failed write says so instead of failing on its columns.
A first full-day run with the 10 + 3.5 GiB split stopped in step 09; run
again, the command skipped the six finished steps and published the day, with
the same results as the undisturbed run. The process that directs the work
used at most `r num(max(dm$driver_java_rss_max_mib))` MiB, and its pod at most
`r num(max(dm$pod_anon_max_mib))` of `r num(dm$pod_limit_mib[1])` MiB.

## Limits

- One day was measured. A busier day takes longer.
- In the first round steps 01, 02 and 02a were scaled, not measured (about
  `r num(100 * (S("01", "after_s") + S("02", "after_s") + S("02a", "after_s")) / after_total)`%
  of the time after the changes). They were measured on the whole day in the
  settings round, above.
- The scaled figure for step 01 may be too low. In a separate study, reading
  `r num(3 * 24)` hours of the archive for only the
  `r num(ar$value[ar$metric == "study_aircraft"])` aircraft that sent ADS-C
  reports that day took `r num(pt$shared_inputs[pt$step == "01"])` s on 12
  executors ([ADS-C study](../adsc-effect-v1/index.qmd)). That run is not a
  daily step 01, which reads one day for all aircraft, but it suggests that
  reading the archive costs more than the 4-hour slice shows.
- The "after" figures of the scaled steps assume that 12 executors are 1.5
  times as fast as 8. For step 02 on one aircraft in 24, 12 executors took
  `r num(ST("m24e12", "02"))` s against `r num(ST("m24new", "02"))` s with 8:
  on a part that small, more executors do not help, which is why the scaling
  goes by cores and not by measured time.

## Provenance

Every number and table on this page is read from the CSV files in `data/` when
the page is rendered; nothing is computed on a cluster, and the page needs no
credentials. The files were written by `benchmarks/day_timing.py` (times per
step and per Spark stage) and `benchmarks/day_compare.py` (comparison of the
outputs) of the opdi repository. `content_comparison.csv` holds the row-by-row
comparison of steps 01 to 02a, `repeat_run_comparison.csv` the two runs of
steps 03 to 09, and `repeat_run_flight_list.csv` the two runs of step 03 with
the sorted list of other airports. `data/_manifest.json` records, for each file,
the script, the git commit, whether the working copy had uncommitted changes
and a fingerprint of the source files. In `step_timings.csv` the run labels
are: `base` the old code, `v1` the new code with 8 executors, `v2` the new
code with 12 executors; `s2`/`s4` are the 2- and 4-hour slices and `m12`/`m24`
the aircraft samples (`base` and `new` for old and new code). The caution on
step 01 reads `papers/adsc-effect-v1/data/processing_time.csv`.

The settings round adds: `settings_tests.csv` (every setting tried or set
aside, with its runs, times, executor-seconds, executors killed and the
reason for the verdict), `executor_events.csv` (executors added, removed and
killed for memory in each run), `executor_memory.csv` and
`driver_memory.csv` (the highest memory use of an executor per step, and of
the process that directs the work), and the comparisons
`settings_events_*.csv` and `settings_flight_list_*.csv` (each setting
against today's settings), `content_p1a_tracks.csv` and
`content_p1k_tracks.csv` (tracks with the Arrow function and with Kryo),
`fault_injection_*.csv` (the day with two executors deleted against the
undisturbed day), `resumed_day_comparison.csv` (the day that stopped in step
09 and was continued) and `full_day_*.csv` (the day from the archive against
the run from the stored tracks). The round on the shuffle parts of steps 02 and 02a adds
`partition_tests.csv` (one row per run: the number of parts, time,
executor-seconds, spill, shuffle, the largest sort's longest and median task,
the highest memory and local disk of one executor, the highest disk use of the
machine, executors lost, and the comparison of its output with the first run
with 104 parts); its labels are `p<parts><a|b>` for step 02 and `c<parts><a|b>`
for step 02a. Its labels in `step_timings.csv`: `p1b`,
`p1a`, `p1k` (steps 02 and 02a, one aircraft in 12: today's settings, Arrow,
Kryo); `pab`, `pae`, `pas`, `pak` (steps 03 to 09 from the stored tracks:
today's settings, 13 executors, 13 executors and 104 parts, all kept
settings); `orch1`, `orch2`, `orch3` (the whole day through the daily
command: first try, with two executors deleted, undisturbed); `01-d0`,
`01-d1` and `01-seed` are the fetches of 14 June, of 15 June and of the last
hours of 13 June inside step 01.
